name: Plain Silk Scroll (Tố Quyên Quyển)
lore: A bolt of painting silk Diệp Tố Quyên wove herself in Tang Ma Thành and carried to the island in 880. She has hung it in every fight since 905 and has never painted on it. She says it is the only thing she owns that is finished.
build_use: Linh lực sustain and a growing ward on the double: the head's long, calm fight.

name: Cloud-Washing Brush (Tẩy Vân Bút)
lore: Kha Đạm Mặc's brush, a wolf-hair tip on a Vạn Can Lâm cane, washed in the pool of Đàm Ảnh Thành every evening from 800 to 1010. It was found floating at the pool's edge the morning after he walked in (N-nhan_van-02). Its strokes fly like needles and leave the ink wet on what they hit.
build_use: The head's attack: quick Water strokes that keep Wood stacks on the foe.
exception: world-depth signature item: its base's common art or ward until an authored one is ruled (review R6)

name: Pool House Mirror (Ảnh Đường Kính)
lore: A round bronze mirror hung opposite the studio window of the Pool House in Đàm Ảnh Thành, so that the room has two skies, the pool's and its own. Mễ Phù Vân takes it down to fight and puts it back crooked, and the painters straighten it.
build_use: Sustain and stronger reflection stacks for the Pool House keeper.
made_by: the bronze-smiths of Tử Điện Thành, for Kha Đạm Mặc

name: Scroll of the Upside-Down Sky (Đảo Thiên Quyển)
lore: The last scroll Tần Vãn Kính finished before the winter of 1158: the sky over Đàm Ảnh Thành painted upside down, as the pool shows it, with one small figure standing on the clouds. Her daughter carries it and has never said who the figure is.
build_use: A young painter's first named piece.

name: Robe of One Cloud a Day (Nhất Nhật Nhất Vân Bào)
lore: A painter's robe of undyed silk on which she paints one small cloud each morning and washes it out each evening. The cloth has held nearly a hundred thousand clouds.
build_use: The idle cloud's body: linh lực, and hard to wear down.

name: Mother's Portrait Brush (Mẫu Họa Bút)
lore: The fine brush Tần Vãn Kính painted faces with, found in her water jar the morning after the winter of 1158. Its tip is still black with the last ink.
